diagnosis: promptly detecting and reporting human or animal infections
treatment: no vaccine or cure for dracunculiasis
transmission: drinking stagnant water contaminated by parasite-infected water fleas
consuming raw or undercooked aquatic hosts harbouring the infective larvae
prevention: promoting the use of cloth or pipe filters in the absence of safe drinking water
discouraging contact with contaminated sources when worms emerge
regularly applying temephos (Abate®) to stagnant water to kill infected water fleas
highlighting the importance of early case detection and reporting
proper management of aquatic animals' waste
risk_factors: relying on open, stagnant water sources for drinking-water
key_facts: 5 countries – Angola, Chad, Ethiopia, Mali, and South Sudan – remain endemic
Sudan is currently in the pre-certification stage
Cameroon is a certified country experiencing a cross-border transmission at its extreme-northern border with Chad
